items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Coleman Hawkins would be having a drink with whoever, Nat King Cole.

ctx.x: Well that’s one reason that I think it’s important that we get stories on tape so that people can find out what it was really like.

Boy if you could have had a microphone, you mentioned 52nd Street, everybody would go play a set and then they’d go ‘round the corner on Sixth Avenue on the southeast corner around facing Sixth Avenue to a place called the White Rose. And boy that was like you died and went to heaven. All your dream people were in there, you know, Coleman Hawkins would be having a drink with whoever, Nat King Cole. It was just marvelous, that era. And to think we took them all for granted, you know. Nobody, that’s one of the…
Well, Milt would need a van.
